DI G BAGONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City SEP 16 2025 www.dilg.gov.ph OPINION NO. JOMER ALEJANDRO A. CRUZ Punong Barangay, Guitnang Bayan I San Mateo, Rizal Dear Hon. Cruz: This has reference to your letteri requesting for the Department's guidance regarding the Ombudsman Order dated February 18, 2025, placing you under preventive suspension for a period not exceeding six (6) months without pay, pending the resolution of the administrative case filed against you. You further informed this Department that you have filed a Motion for Reconsideration in an effort to stay the implementation of said Order. In this regard, you seek appropriate guidance on the available legal interventions in light of applicable laws and regulations. At the outset, it must be emphasized that DILG Memorandum Order No. 2010-02 dated September 17, 2010, proscribes the Department from rendering opinions on the following matters: 1. Those containing facts that are justiciable in nature. Justiciable issues are those that require adjudication by the courts of law as to who between the opposing parties have the better right over the given controversy; 2. Those presumptively valid acts, e.g. enacted ordinances, consummated acts that already enjoy the presumption of regularity on the part of the public officer concerned, and similar instances; 3. Those that are litis pendencia or pending litigation, except when the court itself requests for the opinion. In the event that an opinion has been rendered by the Department and its field officers without knowledge or information that a case involving the issues raised in the query is pending in court, such opinion shall automatically be deemed ineffective, and those that are cognizable by other agencies of the government. In view of the foregoing and considering that your case is already pending before the Office of the Ombudsman, this Department is prohibited from issuing a legal opinion on the merits of the matter to avoid violating the sub judice rule and internal policy. Without delving into the specific facts of your case, and solely for purposes of academic discussion and general guidance, we deem it appropriate to set forth the applicable legal framework on the matter of preventive suspension. March 6, 2025 "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

Preventive suspension is not a form of penalty but a precautionary measure intended to ensure the integrity of an ongoing administrative investigation. It is imposed to prevent a public officer from using their position to influence witnesses, tamper with evidence, or otherwise interfere with the investigative process. Under Section 24 of Republic Act No. 6770, otherwise known as the Ombudsman Act of 1989, the Ombudsman or his Deputy may preventively suspend any officer or employee under his authority pending an investigation, if in his judgment the evidence of guilt is strong, and (a) the charge against such officer or employee involves dishonesty, oppression or grave misconduct or neglect in the performance of duty: (b) the charges would warrant removal from the service; or (c) the respondent's continued stay in office may prejudice the case filed against him. The preventive suspension shall continue until the case is terminated by the Office of the Ombudsman but not more than six (6) months, without pay, except when the delay in the disposition of the case by the Office of the Ombudsman is due to the fault, negligence or petition of the respondent, in which case the period of such delay shall not be counted in computing the period of suspension herein provided. Simply put, the suspension shall not exceed six (6) months without pay, unless the delay in the disposition of the case is attributable to the fault, negligence, or actions of the respondent. Moreover, under Section 7, Rule Ill of Administrative Order No. 07, as reiterated in Ombudsman Memorandum Circular No. 01, s. 2006, it is provided that: "Section 7 Rule Ill of Administrative Order No. 07, otherwise known as, the "Ombudsman Rules of Procedure" provides that: "A decision of the Office of the Ombudsman in administrative cases shall be executed as a matter of course. " In order that the foregoing rule may be strictly observed, all concerned are hereby enjoined to implement all Ombudsman decisions, orders or resolutions in administrative disciplinary cases, immediately upon receipt thereof by their respective offices The filing of a motion for reconsideration or a petition for review before the Office of the Ombudsman does not operate to stay the immediate implementation of the foregoing Ombudsman decisions, orders or resolutions. Only a Temporary Restraining Order (TRO) or a Writ of Preliminary Injunction, duly issued by a court of competent jurisdiction, stays the immediate implementation of the said Ombudsman decisions, orders or resolutions. " In light of the foregoing, and without passing upon the merits or specific facts of your case, it is the Department's considered view that: 1. Preventive suspension orders issued by the Office of the Ombudsman are immediately executory, notwithstanding the filing of a motion for reconsideration; and Page 2 0f3

2. Such orders may only be stayed by the issuance ofa TRO or Writ of Preliminary Injunction by a court of competent jurisdiction. For any further concerns pertaining to your case, we strongly recommend that you consult your legal counsel, who is in the best position to assess your legal options based on the particular facts and circumstances involved. This opinion is rendered without prejudice to any contrary position of competent authorities or final ruling of the courts. We hope to have provided helpful guidance on the matter. Very truly yours, IZß-z- ATTY. ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLA,'RPB/LLLS-LLRALD/rnag/kbm Page 3 0f3
